## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Daṇḍadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 528) is a Pali verse text belonging to the *Therāpadāna* section of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Like many biographical poems in the *Apadāna*, it recounts the past meritorious deed and subsequent spiritual fruition of an elder (thera) who offered a walking staff or stick (*daṇḍa*). While no dedicated secondary studies or textual discussions are included in the research dossier, SuttaCentral indexes translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallels in other Buddhist canonical traditions are identified by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread formulaic text reuse within the Pali canon, recording 122 matching passages across 58 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its opening verses closely match another homonymous poem in the collection, the earlier *Daṇḍadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 357, segment range §0.2–3.4) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, standard clausal sequences and stock verse blocks (§3.1–8.1) are shared extensively with other *Apadāna* accounts, including the two poems titled *Mañcadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 422 and Tha-Ap 524), *Labujadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 384), and *Ghatamaṇḍadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 428 and 498), as well as the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records weak algorithmic alignment with the Tibetan translation of the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2), though with a low plausibility score [DharmaNexus].
